title: Preregistration frozen for phase 2
conclusion: Rivals, discriminating predictions, falsifiers, indeterminate outcomes, negative controls and decision rules were written and schema-validated before any new measurement. P7-LICENSING was moved out of the matrix into the compliance section because a licensing condition has no scientific rival.

title: Harness validity control NC-HARNESS
conclusion: A regenerated six-step output at the locked prompt and seed 101 reproduces the stored locked reference to the recorded precision. The harness is valid. An earlier apparent failure at DINO 0.8665 was a seed error: the bench default is 42 while the lock is 101.

title: Step-count quality curve locates the cliff between three and two steps
conclusion: Six to three steps costs 0.065 DINO while three to two costs 0.384 on this cell. The cliff is between three and two steps. Single cell only, and the twelve-cell re-measurement in run 51 shows this cell is a favourable draw.

title: Twelve-cell step-count comparison: three equals four, two is bimodal, one is non-functional
conclusion: Three steps matches four steps on mean and median for one fewer denoiser call. Two steps has a heavy failure tail: median 0.7813 but mean 0.6456 and min 0.1445. One step is uncorrelated with the reference at the median. Every earlier quality number in this project rested on one cell that overstates quality by about 0.10, so the gate must be widened before further training.

title: Two-step sigma grid search: schedule choice explains a large share of the recorded gap
conclusion: Searching the second sigma moved DINO from 0.5503 to 0.8472 on the tuning cell with no training. The earlier correction experiment was trained to compensate for a poor target grid rather than a real student deficiency. The optimum is still at the edge of the searched range, so it is reported as a bound and the range must be widened. Grids starting below sigma 1.0 are rejected by the accepted harness. Per project rule this is an ablation, not a student.

title: Latency floor model: one second is not reachable by step reduction on this card
conclusion: A perfect one-step student lands at about 1.12 s with a short prompt and about 1.34 s on the accepted long-prompt profile, and the floor with no denoising is 0.78 s. The first-call surcharge of 0.2220 s exceeds the entire saving from two steps to one and from four to three, and it is LoRA plus ConvRot fault machinery rather than a quality term. Text encode plus VAE is 0.780 s and no denoiser work touches it.

title: Accepted long-prompt protocol: three steps to two steps buys no measurable latency
conclusion: On the accepted long-prompt protocol, three steps is 0.319 s faster than five and matches four steps in quality, but three to two is 0.009 s which is inside run-to-run spread, while two steps loses 0.19 mean DINO and gains a failure tail. The two-step target is therefore not worth pursuing for latency on this card. Absolute latencies in this session run 20 to 45 percent above the recorded accepted session with no GPU throttling detected, so this session's absolutes are not comparable to accepted numbers and the one-step projection is a lower bound; only within-session ratios are used.
